title: CX-MT043-TurnSteerInterrupt
clause: turn/start with composed input, turn/steer wired to the steer-queue drain (mid-turn, no relaunch), turn/interrupt, TurnItem stream + token usage

scope.summary:
GOAL: Wire the turn layer of the Codex adapter: turn/start with the composed initial input (role overlay + MT payload from the MT-083 composition seam), turn/steer as FIRST-CLASS mid-turn steering driven by the MT-002 steer-queue drain (guidance injected into a RUNNING turn without interrupting or relaunching it), turn/interrupt mapping to an Interrupted turn state, the item.* event stream mapped into a typed TurnItem stream, and token-usage capture from turn.completed. turn/steer vs turn/interrupt is the cleanest published model of steering in the field; Handshake's internal session model (MT-001 family) is mapped onto exactly this shape - this MT is the payoff seam of the whole CX group.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/codex_app_server/turns.rs implementing CodexTurnDriver over the MT-041 client + MT-042 thread adapter, a TurnItem typed stream, the steer-queue bridge, and unit tests. Re-export additions in codex_app_server/mod.rs. No modification to the MT-002 steer-queue seam itself (consumed, not authored).

DETAILED SPEC:
1. TURN START. start_turn(thread, input) calls turn/start with the initial input composed by the MT-083 composition seam (role overlay + MT payload). The composed input arrives as an opaque, already-rendered payload; this MT does NOT compose roles or MT text itself - it only requires that turn/start receives it verbatim and that the turn is associated with the originating mt_id/session ids for recording (MT-045). Only one active turn per thread: starting a turn while one is active is a typed TurnAlreadyActive error (the app-server thread model is sequential turns).
2. STEER BRIDGE (core deliverable). The MT-002 steer queue holds operator/orchestrator guidance targeted at a session. This MT subscribes a drain to that queue for threads owned by this adapter: while a turn is ACTIVE, each drained steer message is delivered via turn/steer against the active turn - guidance is injected MID-TURN, the model sees it at its next step boundary, and the turn is NOT interrupted, NOT relaunched, and its already-streamed items remain valid. Ordering: FIFO per thread; a steer drained while delivery of the previous one is in-flight queues behind it (no reordering, no coalescing unless the MT-002 queue itself coalesces). If NO turn is active when a steer is drained, the message follows the MT-002 policy surface (hold for next turn/start and prepend to its input, or reject-typed if the policy says immediate-only) - the chosen behavior is read from the MT-002 seam's policy field, not invented here. Every steer delivery outcome (delivered-mid-turn, held-for-next-turn, rejected, failed-typed) is reported back to the MT-002 queue entry so the steering operator sees a definitive per-message disposition.
3. INTERRUPT. interrupt_turn(thread) calls turn/interrupt; the turn transitions to Interrupted (a terminal state for that turn; the THREAD stays usable - a subsequent turn/start on the same thread is legal and must be tested). In-flight items at interrupt time are retained with their partial content and marked truncated-by-interrupt. Steer messages still queued for that turn are returned to the MT-002 queue as undelivered-typed (never silently dropped).
4. TURN ITEM STREAM. Subscribe to the MT-041 notification stream and project item.started/item.updated/item.completed for the active turn into a typed TurnItem stream with item kinds: agent_message, reasoning, command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call, web_search, plan_update, plus Unknown{raw} for forward-compatibility. Emission discipline mirrors the exec lane's proven rule (agent_activity.rs lines 301-304): consumers get completed items always, and started markers for long-running kinds (command_execution) so activity is visible before completion. The stream carries thread_id, turn_id, item_id, kind, and the typed payload.
5. TOKEN USAGE. turn.completed carries token usage; capture it into a typed TurnUsage { input_tokens, cached_input_tokens (if present in schema), output_tokens, total } attached to the turn result and forwarded to MT-045 for cost/usage rows. turn.failed (if present in schema) maps to a typed TurnFailed with the server-reported reason.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read the delivered MT-002 steer-queue seam (drain API + no-active-turn policy field + per-message disposition reporting) and the MT-041/MT-042 public APIs in the implementation worktree.
2. Author turns.rs: CodexTurnDriver { client, thread_adapter, steer_drain_handle, item_tx } with start_turn/interrupt_turn/active_turn_state.
3. Implement the single-active-turn state machine (Idle -> TurnActive -> {Completed, Interrupted, Failed}) at thread scope, updating MT-042's thread state on transitions.
4. Implement the TurnItem projection from the MT-041 notification stream per spec item 4 with per-turn filtering (drop-or-buffer rules for items of other threads are: filter by thread_id, never cross-deliver).
5. Implement the steer bridge per spec item 2 incl. disposition reporting and interrupt-time undelivered return.
6. Implement usage capture per spec item 5.
7. Unit-test everything against the MT-041 fake transport with scripted JSONL: mid-turn steer delivery order, steer-while-no-active-turn policy branches, interrupt with queued steers returned undelivered, item stream kinds incl. unknown kind tolerance, usage capture, TurnAlreadyActive, and post-interrupt new-turn legality.
8. Run proof targets; record outputs.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI work in this MT)
MT-002 steer-queue seam modules (consume the drain API; do not modify)
acceptance_criteria: start_turn delivers the composed input verbatim to turn/start and enforces single-active-turn with typed TurnAlreadyActive (tests).

A steer message drained from the MT-002 queue while a turn is active is delivered via turn/steer WITHOUT interrupting the turn: the fake-transport script proves the turn continues streaming items after steer delivery and completes normally (test).
Steer delivery is FIFO per thread; a 3-message burst arrives at the server in drain order (test).
Steer with no active turn follows the MT-002 policy field (both policy branches tested: held-and-prepended to next turn/start; rejected-typed).
Every steer message ends in exactly one reported disposition: delivered-mid-turn, held-for-next-turn, rejected, failed-typed, or undelivered-returned-on-interrupt (test asserts exhaustiveness).

interrupt_turn maps to Interrupted state; partial items are retained marked truncated-by-interrupt; queued steers are returned undelivered-typed; a NEW turn on the same thread afterwards succeeds (tests).
TurnItem stream projects all seven documented item kinds plus Unknown{raw} without panic; items are filtered by thread_id (tests).
TurnUsage is captured from turn.completed and attached to the turn result (test); turn.failed (if schema-present) maps to typed TurnFailed.
MT-042 thread state reflects TurnActive/Interrupted transitions (test).
proof_targets: HSK_CODEX_LIVE=1 cargo test -p handshake_core codex_steer_mid_turn_live -- --nocapture --ignored  # live: steer a real running turn and observe uninterrupted completion; absent CLI/login => typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF, never silent skip
code_surfaces: MT-002 steer-queue seam (consumed: drain API, no-active-turn policy, disposition reporting)
MT-083 composition seam (consumed: opaque composed initial input)
agent_activity.rs lines 49-54 (envelope doc) and 301-304 (emit rule precedent), parse_codex_line at line 284 (exec-lane dialect kept separate)
expected_tests: codex_steer_mid_turn_live (live-gated; typed NEEDS_MANAGED_RESOURCE_PROOF when CLI/login absent)
implementation_notes: turn/steer is the reason the app-server lane exists for Handshake: the exec lane can only relaunch with new prompt text. Never implement steer as interrupt+restart; the acceptance test explicitly proves the turn keeps streaming after steer.

Do not reuse parse_codex_line (agent_activity.rs:284) for app-server notifications - that function parses the exec lane's `codex exec --json` event shapes. The app-server bindings live in MT-041 protocol.rs; MT-045 owns unifying both into recording.
Composed initial input is opaque here: the role overlay + MT payload contract is MT-083's (roles MT-081/082). Assert pass-through byte-equality in tests, nothing more.
Steer disposition reporting is what makes steering observable and attributable for the operator (GLOBAL-BUILD-035..037); wire it to the MT-002 entry, and MT-045 records it to FR.
Field names for usage (input_tokens/cached_input_tokens/output_tokens) must be taken from the generated schema at implementation time; keep Option-al fields for schema variance.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless backend adapter MT: no operator-visible surface changed; visual verification = TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004.

target_entries: Codex lane: mid-turn steering (what turn/steer does, when a steer is held vs delivered vs rejected, how dispositions read)
Codex lane: interrupting a turn (state outcome, partial items, queued-steer return, thread reusability)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Turn start/steer-disposition/interrupt/complete are FR business events; kind mapping finalized in MT-045 with MT-161 kinds.
Recorded DEFERRED-with-reason if internal_diagnostics is not present in the implementation worktree at claim time; never silently skipped.
Turn liveness rides the MT-041 health probe + MT-005 supervisor; external-watcher registration deferred there; recorded, never silently skipped.

risk_if_missed: No mid-turn steering: operator guidance can only interrupt-and-relaunch Codex turns, losing in-flight work and defeating the WP's core steering goal; MT-044/045/047 lose their turn substrate.

risks: RISK-1: Steer-as-interrupt fake - implementing steer by interrupting and restarting the turn would pass naive tests while destroying in-flight work (the exact deflection this MT exists to prevent).
RISK-2: Lost/dropped steers - a steer drained but never delivered (turn ended racing the drain) disappears silently; the operator believes guidance was applied.
RISK-3: Cross-thread item leakage - items of thread A projected into thread B's TurnItem stream corrupt transcripts and steering context.
RISK-4: Reorder under burst - concurrent steer deliveries arriving out of order invert operator intent ("stop X, then do Y" becomes "do Y, then stop X").
RISK-5: Usage loss on interrupt/failure - token usage only captured on clean completion undercounts cost rows.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Acceptance test scripts items AFTER steer delivery within the SAME turn_id and asserts normal completion; live MT-047 steer test repeats this against the real CLI.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Exhaustive disposition contract - every drained steer must end in exactly one reported disposition incl. undelivered-returned; test asserts no silent path.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): thread_id filtering on the projection with a two-thread interleaved fake-transport test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Per-thread FIFO with in-flight serialization (next delivery awaits previous ack); burst-order test.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Capture usage from turn.completed AND from the terminal notification of interrupted/failed turns when the schema provides it; absent data recorded as typed-unknown, not zero.
